version.changelog: Add dual scoring (optimistic vs realistic), single falsifying assumption

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed business-planning helper that reads project context and writes structured canvas documents, with no evidence of hidden execution, exfiltration, or persistence.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to read README, AGENTS.md, product descriptions, existing business docs, and codebase capabilities; this is proportionate to creating a product/business canvas but users should expect local project inspection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no executable scripts, dependencies, remote payloads, or install-time behavior observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation phrases include broad terms like "business model," but the runtime flow asks the user to confirm project understanding before proceeding and stays within business-modeling tasks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to creating or updating Markdown documents under docs/business/ and optional changelog sections; there is no background worker, privilege escalation, credential use, or system-level persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to generate Business Model Canvas, Value Proposition Canvas, test cards, and summaries, and the instructions consistently support that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an agent to inspect your project context and help produce business-modeling documents. Review the generated docs before sharing them, especially because they may summarize product strategy, pricing, competitors, and assumptions inferred from your repository.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language is real, but it is still related to business modeling and commercialization; given the confirmation step and low-impact Markdown outputs, this is guidance-level rather than a Review-level concern.
